title: Right adjoints inherit the coefficient comparisons
statement:
Work in the standing coefficient setting of [def-pur-conventions]: fix the global finite-field datum with algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ and its fixed coefficient closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-pc-scheme]; no absolute separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ is required. Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a coefficient extension between admissible stages $A_{E,n}$ ($n\ge1$), $\mathcal O_E$, $E$, or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with finite extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the fixed closure. Use the coefficient categories $\Dctf(T,\Lambda)$ of [def-sf-categories]. Assume extension of scalars supplies functors $T^X:\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$ and $T^Y:\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(Y,\Lambda')$; subscripts $(-)_{\Lambda'}$ denote these functors on objects and morphisms. Let $F=Rf_{!,\Lambda}$ and $F'=Rf_{!,\Lambda'}$ be the given compact-support functors between the respective $X$- and $Y$-categories. Fix right adjoints $G=f^!_\Lambda$ and $G'=f^!_{\Lambda'}$ with counits $\varepsilon_f$ and $\varepsilon'_f$. Suppose
$$b(M):T^Y(FM)\xrightarrow{\sim}F'(T^XM)$$
is natural in $M$. Let $J$ and $J'$ be any other right adjoints of $F$ and $F'$, with counits $\varepsilon^J$ and $\varepsilon^{J'}$. For $K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, define $c_J(K):T^X(JK)\to J'(T^YK)$ as the $J'$-transpose of
$$T^Y(\varepsilon^J_K)\circ b(JK)^{-1}:F'(T^X(JK))\to T^YK,$$
where transposition under $F'\dashv J'$ sends $h:A\to J'B$ to $\varepsilon^{J'}_B\circ F'(h)$ [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity]. Define $c_f(K):T^X(GK)\to G'(T^YK)$ by the same rule for $G,G'$. Let $\gamma:G\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ and $\gamma':G'\xrightarrow{\sim}J'$ be the counit-compatible isomorphisms of [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Then
$$c_J(K)=\gamma'_{T^YK}\circ c_f(K)\circ T^X(\gamma_K^{-1}).$$
Consequently $c_J(K)$ is an isomorphism whenever $c_f(K)$ is. The maps $c_J,c_f$ are natural in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

For a chain $\Lambda_0\to\Lambda_1\to\Lambda_2$, make the same choices $F_i\dashv G_i=f^!_{\Lambda_i}$, $F_i\dashv J_i$ at each stage, with coefficient functors $T^X_{ij},T^Y_{ij}$ and comparisons $b_{ij}$ for $ij=01,12,02$. Use the same $J_1$ and $G_1$ in both adjacent comparisons. Let $a^X:T^X_{12}T^X_{01}\xrightarrow{\sim}T^X_{02}$ and $a^Y:T^Y_{12}T^Y_{01}\xrightarrow{\sim}T^Y_{02}$ be the specified natural identifications of successive scalar extensions. If $c_f$ obeys the composition identity
$$G_2(a^Y_K)\circ c_{f,12}(T^Y_{01}K)\circ T^X_{12}(c_{f,01}(K))=c_{f,02}(K)\circ a^X_{G_0K},$$
then $c_J$ obeys the identical equation with $G_i,c_{f,ij}$ replaced by $J_i,c_{J,ij}$. With the identifications suppressed, this is the composition identity for $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$ in the source.

proof.text:
Write $\varepsilon_f$ for the counit of $F\dashv G$ and $\varepsilon'_f$ for that of $F'\dashv G'$. Applying [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to $(F,G,J)$ and $(F',G',J')$ gives natural isomorphisms with
$$\varepsilon^J_K\circ F(\gamma_K)=\varepsilon_{f,K},\qquad \varepsilon^{J'}_B\circ F'(\gamma'_B)=\varepsilon'_{f,B}.$$
Precompose the first equality with $F(\gamma_K^{-1})$ and use $F(\gamma_K\circ\gamma_K^{-1})=\mathrm{id}$ to obtain $\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ F(\gamma_K^{-1})=\varepsilon^J_K$.

source.place: Counit compatibility of gamma and gamma prime; first and fourth identities in the source proof

proof.text:
Use [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] with $L_1=F$, $L_2=F'$, the vertical functors $T^X,T^Y$, and $\alpha=b^{-1}:F'T^X\to T^YF$. Its mate for right adjoints $J,J'$ is $c_J$, and its mate for $G,G'$ is $c_f$: the transpose formula in that node is precisely the definition in the statement. Thus both are natural transformations. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] to these objectwise transposes gives
$$\varepsilon^{J'}_{T^YK}\circ F'(c_J(K))=T^Y(\varepsilon^J_K)\circ b(JK)^{-1},$$
$$\varepsilon'_{f,T^YK}\circ F'(c_f(K))=T^Y(\varepsilon_{f,K})\circ b(GK)^{-1}.$$
All objects are in the supplied coefficient categories and each transpose is under the supplied target-stage adjunction.

source.place: Definition of c_f and c_J; comparison of J-prime transposes

proof.text:
Put $t=\gamma_K^{-1}:JK\to GK$. Naturality of the given $b$ says $F'(T^Xt)\circ b(JK)=b(GK)\circ T^Y(Ft)$. Precompose by $b(JK)^{-1}$ and postcompose by $b(GK)^{-1}$; this gives the correctly typed equality
$$b(GK)^{-1}\circ F'(T^Xt)=T^Y(Ft)\circ b(JK)^{-1}.$$
Only the inverse equations for the assumed isomorphisms $b(JK)$ and $b(GK)$ are used.

source.place: Naturality of b moves the extended gamma inverse across the compact-support comparison

proof.text:
Set $q_K=\gamma'_{T^YK}\circ c_f(K)\circ T^X(\gamma_K^{-1})$. Functoriality of $F'$, Steps 1 and 2, and then Step 3 give
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^{J'}_{T^YK}\circ F'(q_K)
&=\varepsilon'_{f,T^YK}\circ F'(c_f(K))\circ F'(T^X(\gamma_K^{-1}))\\
&=T^Y(\varepsilon_{f,K})\circ b(GK)^{-1}\circ F'(T^X(\gamma_K^{-1}))\\
&=T^Y(\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ F(\gamma_K^{-1}))\circ b(JK)^{-1}\\
&=T^Y(\varepsilon^J_K)\circ b(JK)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is the inverse counit identity of Step 1. It is the transpose of $c_J(K)$ by Step 2. Explicitly, [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity] says that an arrow $h:T^X(JK)\to J'(T^YK)$ with this transpose must equal $J'(T^Y(\varepsilon^J_K)\circ b(JK)^{-1})\circ\eta^{J'}_{T^X(JK)}$. Both $q_K$ and $c_J(K)$ equal that arrow. Hence $q_K=c_J(K)$.

source.place: Equality of the two J-prime transposes and hence equality of the comparison maps

proof.text:
If $c_f(K)$ has inverse $d_K$, then $\gamma'_{T^YK}$ and $T^X(\gamma_K^{-1})$ have inverses $(\gamma'_{T^YK})^{-1}$ and $T^X(\gamma_K)$, respectively. Step 4 therefore supplies an inverse of $c_J(K)$, namely
$$T^X(\gamma_K)\circ d_K\circ(\gamma'_{T^YK})^{-1}.$$
Composing in either order cancels each adjacent inverse pair; the inverse pair after $T^X$ cancels because a functor preserves composition and identities. This proves the isomorphism implication without asserting that a mate of every isomorphism is invertible.

source.place: As gamma and gamma prime are isomorphisms, invertibility transfers

proof.text:
For the chain in the statement, write $\gamma_i:G_i\to J_i$ for [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Substitute Step 4 for $c_{J,12}$ and $c_{J,01}$ in the left side of the desired composition identity. The factors $T^X_{12}(\gamma_{1,T^Y_{01}K}^{-1})$ and $T^X_{12}(\gamma_{1,T^Y_{01}K})$ are adjacent and cancel. Naturality of $\gamma_2$ at the arrow $a^Y_K:T^Y_{12}T^Y_{01}K\to T^Y_{02}K$ says
$$J_2(a^Y_K)\circ\gamma_{2,T^Y_{12}T^Y_{01}K}=\gamma_{2,T^Y_{02}K}\circ G_2(a^Y_K).$$
The left side of the desired identity is consequently
$$\gamma_{2,T^Y_{02}K}\circ G_2(a^Y_K)\circ c_{f,12}(T^Y_{01}K)\circ T^X_{12}(c_{f,01}(K))\circ T^X_{12}T^X_{01}(\gamma_{0,K}^{-1}).$$

source.place: Conjugating the composition identity: the middle gamma-prime factors cancel

proof.text:
Apply the assumed composition identity for $c_f$ to the middle three factors of Step 6. This gives
$$\gamma_{2,T^Y_{02}K}\circ c_{f,02}(K)\circ a^X_{G_0K}\circ T^X_{12}T^X_{01}(\gamma_{0,K}^{-1}).$$
Naturality of the supplied $a^X$ at $\gamma_{0,K}^{-1}:J_0K\to G_0K$ gives
$$a^X_{G_0K}\circ T^X_{12}T^X_{01}(\gamma_{0,K}^{-1})=T^X_{02}(\gamma_{0,K}^{-1})\circ a^X_{J_0K}.$$
Use Step 4 for $02$ to identify the resulting first three factors as $c_{J,02}(K)$. The result is $c_{J,02}(K)\circ a^X_{J_0K}$, the required right side. When the associators are identities the same calculation is literal cancellation; no coherence or composition of $b$ beyond the assumed identity for $c_f$ has been presumed.

lean.statement: theorem det_sp_unique_adjoint_coefficients (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) (f : Arrow Scheme.{u}) [f.left.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [f.right.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (f.left ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [QuasiCompact (f.left ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (f.right ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [QuasiCompact (f.right ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [f.hom.IsOver (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [IsSeparated f.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType f.hom] [QuasiCompact f.hom] (Λ Λ' : AdjointCoefficientStage P) (F : Λ.category f.left ⥤ Λ.category f.right) (F' : Λ'.category f.left ⥤ Λ'.category f.right) (TX : Λ.category f.left ⥤ Λ'.category f.left) (TY : Λ.category f.right ⥤ Λ'.category f.right) (G J : Λ.category f.right ⥤ Λ.category f.left) (G' J' : Λ'.category f.right ⥤ Λ'.category f.left) (adjG : F ⊣ G) (adjJ : F ⊣ J) (adjG' : F' ⊣ G') (adjJ' : F' ⊣ J') (b : F ⋙ TY ≅ TX ⋙ F') : (∀ K : (Λ.category f.right), coefficientRightMate F F' TX TY b J' J adjJ' adjJ K = TX.map ((adjG.rightAdjointUniq adjJ).inv.app K) ≫ coefficientRightMate F F' TX TY b G' G adjG' adjG K ≫ (adjG'.rightAdjointUniq adjJ').hom.app (TY.obj K)) ∧ (∀ K : (Λ.category f.right), IsIso (coefficientRightMate F F' TX TY b G' G adjG' adjG K) → IsIso (coefficientRightMate F F' TX TY b J' J adjJ' adjJ K)) ∧ (∀ (K L : (Λ.category f.right)) (k : K ⟶ L), TX.map (J.map k) ≫ coefficientRightMate F F' TX TY b J' J adjJ' adjJ L = coefficientRightMate F F' TX TY b J' J adjJ' adjJ K ≫ J'.map (TY.map k)) ∧ (∀ (K L : (Λ.category f.right)) (k : K ⟶ L), TX.map (G.map k) ≫ coefficientRightMate F F' TX TY b G' G adjG' adjG L = coefficientRightMate F F' TX TY b G' G adjG' adjG K ≫ G'.map (TY.map k))
